# A USD-denominated sale whose base-currency side has splits both ways: 140.00
# CAD of revenue less a 14.00 CAD discount, against 90.00 USD receivable. The
# CAD booked is 126.00, so the cost of that USD is 126/90 = 1.40 CAD/USD — the
# same rate every split is valued at (share_price 10000/14000).
#
# What this fixture produces: one cost basis, listed by `fx-balances` at
# 1.4 CAD/USD for 90.00 USD.
#
# Contrast it with fx_buy_usd_with_bank_fee.txt, where a 2.70 CAD fee is NOT
# part of what the currency cost. The difference is what the base-currency
# split is: a discount reduces the revenue the receivable was posted for, so it
# belongs in the cost; a fee is a separate expense the bank charged, so it does
# not. Both directions matter — counting the fee overstates the basis, ignoring
# the discount understates it, and either way every gain later measured against
# that basis is wrong by the same amount.
#
# Verified by tests/unit/services/test_cost_of_split.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable USD
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Sales
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Discounts
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

2026-01-05 * "USD sale with a CAD discount"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Accounts Receivable USD 90.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "90.00"
	Income:Sales -140.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "10000/14000"
		value: "-100.00"
	Income:Discounts 14.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "10000/14000"
		value: "10.00"
